get.description:
This endpoint returns the Starglass API key of the currently logged-in user.
While you need this API key to issue a request *as* a logged-in user, it
is useful for the Starglass frontend to be able to retrieve the API key in
this way.

If the request is made without authentication, the response will have an
HTTP 401 status code.
get.summary: Get the currently logged-in user's API key

get.description:
Retrieve information about astronomers known to the Starglass database. If no
parameters are provided, information about all known astronomers is returned.
Otherwise, the set of returned information is filtered according to the parameters.

The returned information includes information about their name as used within
Starglass, and "authority names" established by institutions such as the
Library of Congress.

parameters.description: A comma-separated list of astronomer names, used to filter the output.
parameters.name: astronomers

get.summary: Get information about astronomers in the Starglass database

get.description:
Retrieve information about plate classes known to the Starglass database. If no
parameters are provided, information about all known plate classes is returned.
Otherwise, the set of returned information is filtered according to the
parameters.

The returned information includes a textual description and a count of the
number of plates annotated as belonging to the class, according to the Starglass
database. Be aware that the plate class information in the database is highly
incomplete and not well-vetted.

parameters.description: A comma-separated list of class IDs, used to filter the output.
parameters.name: class

get.description:
Retrieve a DASCH photometric calibration data asset. Rather than returning any
content, this API endpoint returns a HTTP redirection response that forwards the
caller to a presigned AWS S3 link to the relevant data file. This link can be used
to download the data file using standard HTTP techniques.

The asset in question is a compilation of photometric calibration metadata stored
in the ASDF container format. Typical file sizes are tens of megabytes. See the DASCH
DR7 documentation for a detailed discussion of the file structure and contents.

Each photcal ASDF file is identified by a unique 32-character hexadecimal identifier.
These identifiers can be obtained from the results of a call to the
[`POST /dasch/dr7/queryexps`](#/default/daschDr7Queryexps) endpoint. For each plate,
there may be multiple photcal files, one for each photometric reference catalog. Note
that the identifiers are MD5 digests but they are *not* the MD5 digests of the file
contents.

parameters.description: The hexadecimal identifier of the photcal ASDF file to obtain.
parameters.name: hexid

get.summary: Redirect the caller to download a photcal ASDF data file

post.description:
This endpoint retrieves a cutout of a DASCH full-plate mosaic image, centered at
the specified coordinates. Because plates may have multiple exposures, each at
a different sky position, the WCS solution number of the exposure must be specified.
This value can be obtained from the results of a call to the
[`POST /dasch/dr7/queryexps`](#/default/daschDr7Queryexps) endpoint.

The response body is a single JSON string, which in turn contains a base64-encoded
representation of a gzipped FITS file. The cutout is created using a standardized
tangential projection centered at the requested coordinates, twenty arcminutes on
a side. See the DASCH DR7 documentation for a more detailed discussion of the
properties of the resulting FITS file.

An error code will be returned if the input parameters are invalid, the selected plate
does not have a high-precision astrometric solution, or the specified exposure does
not overlap the target projection.
post.summary: Obtain a FITS cutout of a full-plate mosaic

post.description:
Retrieve a table of lightcurve data. Due to the nature of the underlying databases,
the source of interest must be identified with two integers: its "reference number"
and "GSC bin index". These quantities may be obtained from the results of a call
to the [`POST /dasch/dr7/querycat`](#/default/daschDr7Querycat) endpoint. These
numbers are only well-defined relative to the choice of one of the DASCH photometric
reference catalogs.

The response body is a JSON list of strings. This list should be treated as series
of lines of a CSV-encoded text file. The first entry in the list will always be a
header line, providing column names. Each subsequent entry describes a lightcurve
point. See the DASCH DR7 documentation for detailed discussion of the semantics of
the data.
post.summary: Obtain the lightcurve of the specified source

post.description:
This endpoint returns a presigned AWS S3 link that can be used to obtain a DASCH
full-plate "mosaic" FITS image, as well as a variety of metadata that can be combined
with this image to produce a final "value-added" FITS file that has a standardized format
and a variety of useful metadata headers.

The code to do this combination lives in the client-side
[*daschlab*](https://dasch.cfa.harvard.edu/dr7/install-daschlab/) Python package. In principle,
value-added FITS file could be created on the server side, but it is a lot easier to have the
server give the client all of the information that it needs, and have the client do all of
the hard work of manipulating images that are potentially gigabytes in size.

The response body is a complex JSON object. Its detailed contents are not documented here.
For de-facto documentation of how the response may be used, consult the Python module
[`daschlab.mosaics`](https://github.com/pkgw/daschlab/blob/main/daschlab/mosaics.py), which
implements the workflow to create the value-added mosaics.

To simply obtain a presigned URL to download a "base" mosaic file, you can use the endpoints
`GET /plates/p/{plate_id}/mosaic` or `GET /plates/p/{plate_id}/mosaic/download`. However, the
WCS headers in these files may be incorrect, and the files will be missing all of the metadata
provided by this endpoint. If you plan to use the resulting FITS files in scientific contexts,
it is **strongly** recommended that you use the *daschlab* infrastructure.
post.summary: Retrieve information needed to assemble a "value-added" DASCH mosaic FITS file

post.description:
Retrieve a table of photometry data from the specified plate, extracting a spatial
subset centered at the specified coordinates. Because plates may have multiple
exposures, each at a different sky position, the WCS solution number of the exposure
must be specified. This value can be obtained from the results of a call to the
[`POST /dasch/dr7/queryexps`](#/default/daschDr7Queryexps) endpoint. A choice of
photometric reference catalog must also be specified.

The selected subset of data will approximately overlap the footprint of the image
returned by a [`POST /dasch/dr7/cutout`](#/default/DaschDr7Cutout) request with the
same center coordinates. The subsetting is done using simple bounding of RA/dec
values and so may behave badly at the poles.

The response body is a JSON list of strings. This list should be treated as series
of lines of a CSV-encoded text file. The first entry in the list will always be a
header line, providing column names. Each subsequent entry describes a source
detection. See the DASCH DR7 documentation for detailed discussion of the semantics of
the data.
post.summary: Obtain multi-source photometry data from a subset of a single plate

post.description:
Retrieve a table of sources in a DASCH photometric reference source catalog,
based on a cone-search query around the specified coordinates. Actually, the
query would be more properly termed a "box search": sources will be returned
in an approximate square shape on the sky, with a half-size matching the
requested radius.

The response body is a JSON list of strings. This list should be treated as series
of lines of a CSV-encoded text file. The first entry in the list will always be a
header line, providing column names. Each subsequent entry describes a catalog
entry. See the DASCH DR7 documentation for detailed discussion of the semantics of
the data.
post.summary: Query a DASCH source catalog at a sky location

post.description:
Retrieve a table of information about exposures in the DASCH database that intersect
the specified coordinates. Keep in mind that some plates have multiple exposures,
so it is possible for a single plate to appear in the results multiple times if it
has more than one exposure that covers the query location.

This endpoint should return an approximately equal set of plates as the
[`POST /plates/search`](#/default/searchPlates) endpoint, but it returns detailed
information aimed at scientific users of the DASCH data.

The response body is a JSON list of strings. This list should be treated as series
of lines of a CSV-encoded text file. The first entry in the list will always be a
header line, providing column names. Each subsequent entry describes an exposure.
See the DASCH DR7 documentation for detailed discussion of the semantics of the
data.
post.summary: Query the DASCH exposure catalog at a sky location

get.description:
Retrieve information about the status of the Neo4j graph database that backs
the Starglass APIs and service.

The returned information includes a status value and a textual description of its
meaning. This API is use by the Starglass frontend to notify users of the
health of the system.
get.summary: Get information about the status of the Starglass database

get.description:
Retrieve information about observatory locations known to the Starglass database.
If no parameters are provided, information about all known locations is returned.
Otherwise, the set of returned information is filtered according to the parameters.

The returned information includes latitude, longitude, and elevation.

parameters.description: A semicolon-separated list of locations, used to filter the output.
parameters.name: locations

get.description:
Retrieve information about notebooks known to the Starglass database. If no
parameters are provided, information about all known notebooks is returned.
Otherwise, the set of returned notebooks is filtered according to the
parameters.

The returned information includes PHaEDRA notebook identifiers, ADS bibcodes,
a list of notebook authors, and a list of pages (really, image IDs) known to
contain mentions of plates that are in the Starglass system.

parameters.description: A comma-separated list of astronomer names, used to filter the output.
parameters.name: astronomers

get.description:
Retrieve information about a specific astronomer notebook known to the
Starglass database. The notebook is identified by its PHaEDRA ID (for
example: "phaedra2139").

The returned information includes the PHaEDRA notebook identifier, ADS
bibcode, a list of notebook authors, and a list of pages known to contain
mentions of plates that are in the Starglass system.

parameters.description: PHaEDRA ID of the notebook
parameters.name: notebook_id

get.summary: Get information about a specific astronomer notebook

get.description:
Retrieve information about a specific page in an astronomer notebook.
The notebook is identified by its PHaEDRA ID (for example: "phaedra2139").
The page number should be one of the ones listed in the notebook information.

The returned information includes general information about the containing
notebook, the URL of a photograph containing the image of the page, and a list
of plates mentioned on the notebook page. The information about plate mentions
was gathered by citizen scientist volunteers in a Zooniverse project.

parameters.description: PHaEDRA id of the notebook
parameters.name: notebook_id

parameters.description: Page number of the notebook page
parameters.name: page_num

get.summary: Get information about a specific page of an astronomer notebook

get.description:
Retrieve detailed information about multiple plates, as identified
by their Starglass names (for example: "a03393"). The list of plates
to query is specified as a single comma-separated string.

Returned information includes data about photographs of each plate and
its jacket, thumbnails of those photos, DASCH scan mosaics, known
exposures of the plates (including WCS coordinate information about the
exposure locations), mentions of the plates in astronomer notebooks,
and information about the physical state of the plates themselves, such as
whether they had handwritten markings and whether those markings were
erased during the DASCH scanning process.

The returned data also includes summary information about the number of
plates requested, the number that were successfully looked up, and the
number of errors that occured while servicing the request.

parameters.description: A comma-separated list of plate IDs
parameters.name: ids

parameters.description: The ratio to reduce the thumbnail image dimensions by; default is 4
parameters.name: thumbnail_ratio

get.summary: Get detailed information about multiple plates

get.description:
Retrieve detailed information about a specific plate, as identified
by its Starglass name (for example: "a03393").

Returned information includes data about photographs of the plate and
its jacket, thumbnails of those photos, DASCH scan mosaics, known
exposures of the plate (including WCS coordinate information about the
exposure locations), mentions of the plate in astronomer notebooks,
and information about the physical state of the plate itself, such as
whether it had handwritten markings and whether those markings were
erased during the DASCH scanning process.

parameters.description: The ID of the plate to retrieve
parameters.name: plate_id

parameters.description: The ratio to reduce the thumbnail image dimensions by; default is 4
parameters.name: thumbnail_ratio

get.summary: Get detailed information about a specific plate

get.description:
Retrieve a plate photograph data asset. Rather than returning any content, this
API endpoint returns a HTTP redirection response that forwards the caller to a
presigned AWS S3 link to the photograph data file. This link can be used to
download the data file using standard HTTP techniques.

This particular endpoint can be used to download a photograph of a plate jacket
or of the plate itself. Note that the plate photographs are not science-grade
images; for quantitative analysis, only DASCH scan "mosaics" should be used.

Photographs are in JPEG format. Their sizes may range from a few megabytes to
tens of megabytes.

To discover what photographs are available for a given plate, use the
`GET /plate/p/{plate_id}` API endpoint. In particular, some plates have multiple
photographs identified by different values of the "portion" parameter, and this
API will tell you which ones are present for the plate in question. Likewise,
if you do not specify the "image_type" parameter, you might get either a jacket
photograph or a plate photograph.

parameters.description: The portion of the plate to return; one of 'all', 'll', 'lr', 'ul', 'ur', 't', or 'b'.
parameters.name: portion

parameters.description: The type of image to return: either 'plate' or 'jacket'.
parameters.name: image_type

parameters.description: If present, a link to a downsampled thumbnail is returned; otherwise, the full image is returned.
parameters.name: thumbnail_ratio

parameters.description: The ID of the plate to query.
parameters.name: plate_id

get.summary: Redirect the caller to download a plate photograph

get.description:
Get information about a DASCH mosaic data asset associated with a plate.

A "mosaic" is single, science-grade scan of a plate produced by the DASCH project.
(The terminology is somewhat confusing compared to standard astronomical usage;
it arose because each mosaic is constructed from individual 4k-by-4k frames
obtained by the DASCH camera system.) Mosaics are stored in the FITS format.
See the DASCH DR7 documentation for a detailed description of the file contents.

Mosaics come in pairs: full-size and "binned". Binned mosaics have been downsampled
in 16-by-16 pixel blocks to significantly reduce their file size. If you do not
provide any optional parameters to this API, you will get information about the
“binned” version of a mosaic. Set the "bin_factor" parameter to "01" to get information
about its full-size partner.

This API returns basic information about the selected mosaic data asset. Most
notably, this includes a presigned AWS S3 link that can be used to retrieve the
mosaic data using standard HTTP methods. These links are only valid for 15 minutes.
The returned information also includes the size of the mosaic file in bytes.

While you should not need to specify the other optional query parameters, relevant
values for them can be obtained using the `GET /plate/p/{plate_id}` API endpoint.
In principle, there can be multiple DASCH mosaics representing the same plate (beyond
the two binning options), and these are be identified by distinct "mosaic_num" values.
In DR7, each plate has one unique mosaic.

parameters.description: The pixel binning factor of the mosaic to select; either '01' or '16'
parameters.name: bin_factor

parameters.description:
Processing flags acquired during DASCH pipeline processing; one of "", "ww", or
"ww_tnx". This value relates to legacy astrometric calibration progress and should be
ignored in DR7. You should never need to specify it in DR7 queries.
parameters.name: flags

parameters.description:
The pipeline-applied rotation of the mosaic to select; one of 'none', 'r90', 'r180',
or 'r270'. This value does not affect data usage and is not needed in DR7.
parameters.name: rotation

parameters.description: The serial number of the mosaic to select; not needed in DR7.
parameters.name: mosaic_num

parameters.description: The ID of the plate to query.
parameters.name: plate_id

get.summary: Get information about a DASCH FITS "mosaic" of a plate

get.description:
Retrieve a plate mosaic data asset. Rather than returning any content, this
API endpoint returns a HTTP redirection response that forwards the caller to a
presigned AWS S3 link to the mosaic data file. This link can be used to
download the data file using standard HTTP techniques.

A "mosaic" is single, science-grade scan of a plate produced by the DASCH project.
(The terminology is somewhat confusing compared to standard astronomical usage;
it arose because each mosaic is constructed from individual 4k-by-4k frames
obtained by the DASCH camera system.) Mosaics are stored in the FITS format.
Full-resolution mosaic files range from several hundred megabytes to
gigabytes in size, depending on the physical size of the plate. See the DASCH DR7
documentation for a detailed description of the file contents.

Mosaics come in pairs: full-size and "binned". Binned mosaics have been downsampled
in 16-by-16 pixel blocks to significantly reduce their file size. If you do not
provide any optional parameters to this API, you will get information about the
“binned” version of a mosaic. Set the "bin_factor" parameter to "01" to get information
about its full-size partner.

While you should not need to specify the other optional query parameters, relevant
values for them can be obtained using the `GET /plate/p/{plate_id}` API endpoint.
In principle, there can be multiple DASCH mosaics representing the same plate (beyond
the two binning options), and these would be identified by distinct "mosaic_num" values.
In DR7, each plate has one unique mosaic.

parameters.description: The pixel binning factor of the mosaic to select; either '01' or '16'
parameters.name: bin_factor

parameters.description:
Processing flags acquired during DASCH pipeline processing; one of "", "ww", or
"ww_tnx". This value relates to legacy astrometric calibration progress and should be
ignored in DR7. You should never need to specify it in DR7 queries.
parameters.name: flags

parameters.description:
The pipeline-applied rotation of the mosaic to select; one of 'none', 'r90', 'r180',
or 'r270'. This value does not affect data usage and is not needed in DR7.
parameters.name: rotation

parameters.name: mosaic_num

post.description:
This endpoint returns a list of IDs of plates matching the search criteria.
Different elements in the request body describe different criteria. The
returned result represents the logical "AND" of all of the specified criteria.

See also the [`POST /dasch/dr7/queryexps`](#/default/daschDr7Queryexps) endpoint,
which has a broadly similar functionality. That endpoint, however, returns
detailed tabular data suitable for scientific users of DASCH data.

Allowed search criteria include positional matches based on either RA/Dec
coordinates (ICRS) in decimal degrees, or an object name resolvable by SIMBAD.
Note that some plates were exposed multiple times with different telescope
pointings. The positional searches use high-accuracy astrometric solutions from
DASCH when available. In some cases, low-accuracy written logbook information
is used as a fallback.

Other search criteria include: plate series; exposure date; astronomers known
to have mentioned the plate; scanned status; exposure count; and so on.

The search results will by default by sorted by plate ID. They can also be
sorted to have the most-mentioned plates come first.
post.summary: Search for plates matching one or more criteria

get.description:
Retrieve information about plate series known to the Starglass database. If no
parameters are provided, information about all known plate series is returned.
Otherwise, the set of returned information is filtered according to the
parameters.

The returned information includes a textual description, some technical information
about telescope size and plate scale, and a count of the number of plates belonging
to the series, according to the Starglass database.

parameters.description: A comma-separated list of series IDs, used to filter the output.
parameters.name: series
